weeks.title: Third Grade Scholar Launch
weeks.theme: Baseline routines, reading stamina, math fluency, inquiry notebooks, collaboration, and portfolio setup
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do strong third-grade scholars learn with independence and evidence?

weeks.title: Text Evidence and Place Value
weeks.theme: Explicit text evidence, place value to thousands, map grids, community identity, and notebook organization
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do evidence and structure help us explain clearly?

weeks.title: Characters, Traits, and Multiplication Arrays
weeks.theme: Character analysis, trait evidence, equal groups, arrays, life-cycle introductions, and visual design
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do patterns reveal character, number, and living systems?

weeks.title: Informational Text and Area Models
weeks.theme: Main idea, details, multiplication area models, forces, push/pull tests, and community systems
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do readers and mathematicians build meaning from parts?

weeks.title: Opinion Writing and Civic Voice
weeks.theme: Opinion essays, reasons/evidence, multiplication facts, classroom constitution, voting, and debate
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a voice be strong, fair, and supported by evidence?

weeks.title: Division and Fair Sharing
weeks.theme: Division stories, equal shares, fact families, procedural writing, cooperation, and fair exchange
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do we divide fairly and explain our process?

weeks.title: Forces, Motion, and Technical Reading
weeks.theme: Technical text, diagrams, motion investigations, data tables, line plots, and engineering sketches
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can diagrams and data explain motion?

weeks.title: Culture, Folktales, and Multiplication Fluency
weeks.theme: Folktales, central message, culture, multiplication fluency, patterns in music, and maps
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do stories carry wisdom across communities?

weeks.title: Weather, Climate, and Data
weeks.theme: Weather data, climate patterns, graphing, informational writing, measurement, and seasonal safety
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can data help us understand weather and climate?

weeks.title: Multi-Step Word Problems
weeks.theme: Two-step problems, close reading in math, unknowns, bar models, perseverance, and explanation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do we solve complex problems without getting lost?

weeks.title: Prefixes, Suffixes, and Morphology
weeks.theme: Word parts, vocabulary, spelling generalizations, roots, fact fluency, and academic language
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do word parts unlock meaning?

weeks.title: Communities Then and Now
weeks.theme: Local history, timelines, sources, narrative writing, measurement, and community change
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do communities change over time?

weeks.title: Life Cycles and Research Notes
weeks.theme: Life cycles, animal groups, research notes, diagrams, paragraph writing, and source sorting
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do living things grow and change?

weeks.title: Traits, Variation, and Data Displays
weeks.theme: Inherited/acquired traits, variation, bar graphs, explanatory writing, and evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why are living things alike and different?

weeks.title: Fractions as Numbers
weeks.theme: Unit fractions, number lines, equal parts, vocabulary precision, and real-world models
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can fractions be numbers on a line?

weeks.title: Equivalent Fractions and Visual Models
weeks.theme: Equivalent fractions, area models, comparison, explanation, symmetry, and design critique
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can different fractions name the same amount?

weeks.title: Midyear Portfolio and Assessment
weeks.theme: Cumulative review, midterm demonstration, revised writing, math proof, and project audit
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I prove my growth with evidence?

weeks.title: Research Writing Workshop
weeks.theme: Research questions, notes, paragraph structure, source ethics, diagrams, and mini-presentation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do researchers turn questions into trustworthy writing?

weeks.title: Area and Perimeter Design Studio
weeks.theme: Area, perimeter, constraints, city planning, arrays, measurement, and blueprint writing
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do designers use measurement to solve problems?

weeks.title: Poetry, Rhythm, and Measurement
weeks.theme: Poetry, figurative language, rhythm, meter, measurement, sound, movement, and performance
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can patterns make language and music powerful?

weeks.title: Fossils and Earth History
weeks.theme: Fossils, past environments, evidence from rocks, sequence, timelines, and scientific claims
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do clues from the past help us explain Earth history?

weeks.title: Habitats, Adaptations, and Survival
weeks.theme: Habitats, adaptations, food chains, cause/effect text, ecosystem models, and conservation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do organisms survive in changing habitats?

weeks.title: Government, Rights, and Responsibilities
weeks.theme: Local government, rules/laws, rights/responsibilities, persuasive writing, and civic action
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do communities make decisions and protect fairness?

weeks.title: Economics, Resources, and Trade
weeks.theme: Goods/services, producers/consumers, resources, budgets, multiplication/division contexts, and market design
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do choices shape a community economy?

weeks.title: Measurement: Mass, Volume, and Time
weeks.theme: Standard measurement, elapsed time foundations, liquid volume, mass, estimation, and lab records
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do precise measurements help us compare and decide?

weeks.title: Geometry and Quadrilaterals
weeks.theme: Attributes, categories, quadrilaterals, symmetry, perimeter, shape sorting, and geometry vocabulary
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do attributes define and connect shapes?

weeks.title: Reading Across Genres
weeks.theme: Compare fiction, nonfiction, poetry, drama, point of view, theme, and evidence discussion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do readers adjust thinking across genres?

weeks.title: Advanced Multiplication and Division
weeks.theme: Products within 100, division fluency, unknown factors, patterns, mental strategies, and explanations
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do multiplication and division work together?

weeks.title: Fractions in the Real World
weeks.theme: Compare fractions, fraction word problems, measurement fractions, fair-share contexts, and cooking/design
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do fractions help us compare and share fairly?

weeks.title: Environmental Stewardship
weeks.theme: Natural resources, community science, water/soil care, civic responsibility, data, and action proposal
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can evidence guide care for the Earth?

weeks.title: Biography and Leadership
weeks.theme: Biography, timelines, leadership traits, point of view, opinion writing, and public speaking
weeks.essentialQuestion: What can we learn from people who lead and serve?

weeks.title: Innovation, Tools, and Engineering
weeks.theme: Engineering design, prototypes, constraints, failures, tool safety, algorithms, and presentation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do inventors improve a design?

weeks.title: Digital Citizenship and Data Tools
weeks.theme: Online safety, ethical creation, keyboarding, spreadsheets, graphs, citations, and digital presentation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can digital tools help us create responsibly?

weeks.title: Big Question Capstone Research
weeks.theme: Independent research, project planning, data/evidence collection, draft, model, and conference
weeks.essentialQuestion: What big question can I investigate deeply?

weeks.title: Capstone Studio and Public Presentation
weeks.theme: Final project, writing revision, math evidence, visual design, oral presentation, and peer questions
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I present evidence clearly and confidently?

weeks.title: Final Review and Grade 4 Readiness
weeks.theme: Cumulative final, portfolio defense, celebration, certificate, transition skills, and reflection
weeks.essentialQuestion: How am I ready for fourth grade?

requires: Weekly assessment average at or above 80%
Portfolio evidence approved by adult mentor
